bull.b: Ally’s expanding customer base and substantial retail deposit funding support a durable digital banking franchise. A larger, relationship-based deposit platform can provide recurring funding for lending growth and reduce reliance on market-based sources over time.

Revenue growth, higher earning-asset expectations, and improving net interest margin indicate stronger operating momentum across the lending platform. Management’s confidence in a sustainable upper-3% margin could support durable earnings growth if asset expansion continues.

Record corporate finance earnings and strong portfolio growth show that Ally has a meaningful business beyond consumer auto lending. The reported return on equity and disciplined underwriting support a potentially attractive, scalable source of diversified earnings.

bear.b: Persistently elevated leverage reduces financial flexibility and leaves less room to absorb weaker profitability or credit performance. It can also constrain capital allocation choices because a larger share of resources must support the balance sheet and funding structure.

Thin and inconsistent free cash flow makes cash generation less dependable than operating cash flow alone suggests. This can limit internally funded capital deployment and make shareholder returns or growth investment more sensitive to balance-sheet and funding conditions.

Reserve builds and still-elevated delinquencies show that credit costs remain an important earnings risk as Ally expands its asset base. Further deterioration in consumer affordability or portfolio performance could increase provisions and offset benefits from growth and margin expansion.
